root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional visibility on click events within its own module. Keyboard navigation triggers change events on radios in a separate module (opt-out) that shares the same radio group name, but the component instance with conditionals doesn't listen for those change events, so the conditional field remains visible.
repair_strategy: In the radios component's init, detect if the module has any conditional radios (with aria-controls). If so, listen for change events on all radios sharing the same name across the document, and update conditionals in this module whenever any radio in the group changes. Also refactor the click handler into a shared updateConditionals method used by both click and change events.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation (arrow keys) between radio options in the same group, including across separate module containers, will correctly show/hide conditional fields, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Duplicate updateConditionals calls when both click and change events fire for the same interaction (idempotent, so safe).
If multiple modules with conditionals share the same radio name, each would add change listeners and update their own conditionals, which is desired.
The _govukRadiosChangeListener property on radio elements could conflict with other scripts, but unlikely.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the email radio to the text radio hides the email input and shows the mobile number input.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the text radio to the opt-out radio hides the mobile number input.
Verify that mouse clicks still correctly show/hide the associated conditional fields.
Verify that the aria-expanded attribute on each radio reflects its checked state after keyboard selection.
Verify that the form data for reminder is correctly set to "none" after opting out.
